events.text: Customer C13171 message: 'I never made this $55.68 purchase. Please check my card.' Refers to 3558054.

events.msg: Core toolkit: flagged transaction, card window, card baseline, recurring charges, resolved account history, device neighbours, region activity and prior cases

hypotheses: The transaction is a legitimate recurring subscription charge that the customer has forgotten or failed to recognize.
The card has been compromised, and an unauthorized party is exploiting the card for recurring or one-off unauthorized purchases.
The transaction is friendly fraud, where a family member or associate of the cardholder made the purchase using a known device.

calls.why: To review the full transaction history on this card to see if there are other unrecognized charges or if the device usage pattern is consistent.
To identify all previous transactions on this card matching the $55.68 amount within a 1% tolerance to confirm a recurring subscription pattern.

events.msg: Four specialist analysts reviewing their evidence in parallel

events.assessment: The customer C13171 has explicitly reported transaction 3558054 ($55.68) as unauthorized, indicating a clear case of card-not-present fraud. The transaction was executed using a generic browser signature and lacked address verification details, which is common in fraudulent card-not-present transactions.
key_points: Customer C13171 confirmed they did not authorize transaction 3558054 for $55.68 on card C13171-K2.
The flagged transaction 3558054 utilized a generic device profile (' |  | chrome 66.0 | ') which is shared across many users and prevents unique device identification.
The transaction had missing address fields (addr1 and addr2 empty) and d1/d15 values of 0, indicating no established history for this specific card configuration.

events.assessment: Customer C13171 has disputed transaction 3558054 ($55.68) as unauthorized. key_points: Customer C13171 disputed transaction 3558054 ($55.68) stating they did not authorize it.
The account C13171-K2||170 shows three prior transactions (3555768, 3556719, and 3557118) on the same day, 2016-12-19, using different device signatures.
The flagged device profile ' |  | chrome 66.0 | ' is a generic browser signature and does not provide sufficient evidence of a specific device takeover or ring activity.

events.assessment: The transaction 3558054 is reported as unauthorized by customer C13171. Although the transaction is linked to a device profile shared by 175 cards, this high volume indicates a generic browser signature rather than a coordinated fraud ring or shared device network.
key_points: Customer C13171 reported transaction 3558054 ($55.68) as unauthorized.
The device profile associated with the transaction is shared by 175 cards all-time, indicating a generic browser signature.

events.assessment: Customer C13171 has reported an unauthorized transaction of $55.68 (ID 3558054). This customer has an extensive history of confirmed fraud cases on card C13171-K2, primarily involving card-not-present transactions from unrecognized devices. Given this recurring pattern, the current alert is highly likely to be another instance of card-not-present fraud.
key_points: Customer C13171 has seven prior confirmed fraud cases (including CC-4485, CC-4163, CC-2244, CC-2454, CC-0467, CC-2059, and CC-0772) on card C13171-K2.
The majority of these historical cases were classified under the 'card_not_present_new_device' pattern, involving unauthorized online purchases from various new mobile and desktop devices.
Only one prior case (CC-4819) was cleared as legitimate after the customer confirmed the purchase from a new phone.

events.claim: The device profile ( |  | chrome 66.0 | ) was already used 9 times on this card before the alert
$55.68 is a typical amount for this card (percentile 68%)
The same amount (+/-1%) recurs on this card on the same day of the month: 2016-11-19 $55.54 (7 matching charge(s) in the last six months), consistent with a recurring charge

This card has 1 earlier alert(s) that were cleared as false alarms (CC-4819; latest note: "Case CC-4819: model scored a $66.52 transaction at 0.92. Cardholder confirmed the purchase from a new phone. Device added to profile. Alert ")

initial.reason: Section 3a: the customer disputes a charge
R7: the disputed charge matches the card's own recurring pattern (same amount, monthly); confirm before any block
R7: send a recurring-charge reminder showing the earlier matching charges

confirm.reason: Section 3a: keep the case record; customer confirmation noted
R3: the customer recognised the recurring charge

deny.reason: R2: customer maintains the charge is unauthorised after seeing the recurring history; exposure $149.86 is under $2,500
Section 3a: fraud confirmed or strongly suspected; record the investigation and write it to the graph

no_reply.reason: R4: no reply within 24 hours; raise monitoring for 72 hours

events.assumed_response: Customer reviews the earlier matching charges and recognises the payment as their own recurring charge

final.reason: Section 3a: keep the case record; customer confirmation noted
R3: the customer recognised the recurring charge

events.what_would_change_verdict: If the customer denied the transaction after reviewing the recurring charges, the verdict would change to fraud, requiring BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE under R2.
